chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Ishaq al-Tajir narrated to us from Ali b. Mahziyar from Fadala b. Ayyub from Ismail b. Abi Ziyad from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever wishes for something whilst being pleased with Allah — Mighty and Majestic — will not leave this world until he is granted it.

key_terms.تمنى: Wished, desired — implies a heartfelt longing or aspiration
key_terms.رضا: Pleasure, contentment — specifically being pleased with and accepting of Allah's will
key_terms.عز وجل: Mighty and Majestic — honorific formula for God
key_terms.يعطاه: Will be granted it — divine bestowal of the desired thing

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about wishes made while being pleased with Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (as) from the Prophet (s), promises that sincere wishes made in a state of divine pleasure and contentment will be fulfilled before death. The teaching encourages believers to align their desires with what pleases God, cultivating a state of rida (divine contentment). The phrase 'while being pleased with Allah' (وهو لله رضا) indicates that the condition for this promise is that the wisher's heart is in a state of acceptance of God's decree, not merely that the wish itself is religiously permissible.
